Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka need 325 to salvage some pride while England will bank themselves to defend this total. Let's see what we have in store. Join us back in a bit for the run chase.

The fielding side were not very successful in their attack as Gunathilaka took honours with his 3 wickets and superb bowling figures. The other bowlers were no slouches as the spinners heavily restricted the English batsmen. However, they were unable to get wickets at a steady pace and despite their spirited fielding, were unable to stop the flow of boundaries.
Root walked in and went on to the anchor the majority of the innings. Buttler matched him for a while and they set up a stand of 109 runs in 86 balls until Buttler was caught and bowled by Bandara.

England end their innings on a respectable 324/7 after a lukewarm yet steady batting performance. After winning the toss, a bit of rain dampened the proceedings but it soon dissipated and the match got underway without the loss of any overs. Roy and Vince got off to a rapid start, bringing up 50 runs in 8.3 overs. However, Roy was caught out by Perera and the 67-run partnership was broken.

Team changes - Chaminda Bandara replaces Farveez Maharoof for Sri Lanka and James Vince and Chris Jordan come in for Alex Hales and Moeen Ali.

TOSS - Sri Lanka win the toss and opt to bowl, breaking England's streak of bowling in the past four matches. There was a slight spell of rain after the toss, causing the covers to be briefly brought on, but the skies have cleared up and the forecast looks promising for the rest of the day.

The Lankans finally hit their stride in the previous match but, between the rain and Jason Roy's fireworks, they were unable to resist the English tide. Will they manage to redeem themselves and play for honour or will England continue to rampage over the tourists?

Hello and a warm welcome to the fifth and final match of the ODI series between England and Sri Lanka. The two sides have faced each other in four ODI matches so far with two ending inconclusively and the Englishmen have won the other two, effectively clinching the series. This has not been a good tour for the visitors as they were whitewashed in the Test series and run the risk of suffering another in the ODI series.
